# Summary of the Cairn System

## Basic Pulse Mechanics
When you apply a pulse to a cairn, it grows in two ways:
- You add a fixed amount called the stride
- You gain bonus growth equal to how many complete stride-sized chunks fit into the cairn's current height

The taller your cairn already is, the more it benefits from each pulse. This creates accelerating growth—height feeds back into itself.

## Multiple Pulses
Each pulse recalculates from scratch. You can't reuse a bonus from a previous pulse because the height has changed. Every pulse uses the new current height to determine its bonus.

## Leaks
A leak happens after a pulse completes. The amount lost depends on the new height (after the pulse), not the starting height. You count how many leak-sized sections fit into that final height and lose that many marks. Leaks can significantly reduce gains, especially when the pulse bonus is modest.

## Drains
Drains are constant—they remove the same fixed amount every cycle, regardless of height. Over time, as the cairn shrinks from repeated drains, the pulse bonus decreases while the drain stays the same. Eventually the pulse adds less than the drain removes, and the cairn empties.

## Finding Origins
To find a starting height before multiple pulses, work backwards through each pulse one at a time. For each pulse, test different heights until you find which one would produce the final result. Use that as your new target and repeat.

## Merging
When combining two cairns, each contributes a percentage of its height (rounded down). There's also a tether bonus based on the shorter cairn—multiply the tether value by that shorter height divided by 10. The tether can be positive (rewarding diverse sizes) or negative (penalizing merges).
